findings.reason: the exemption was added to answer exactly this path, and as written it covers only the detector's own invalidation, so an implementer follows the plan to a guard that never holds on the streamed read the sentence names; the plan must either name the change-stream handler's invalidation as exempt too or key the guard to the detector's recorded pass rather than to a per-tree invalidation timestamp, and the difference is invisible to the node's gate because its test calls `index_rows` directly.
findings.text: §15's trust guard exempts "the invalidation the pass itself fires, which the change stream's own read follows at once", but the change-stream handler fires an invalidation of its own before it reads: `reckon/serve.py:2805` calls `_invalidate_tree_views(docs_dir, changed_at=changed_at)` and `:2806` then reads `rows = _served_index_rows(docs_dir, project)` in the same loop iteration, with its own `changed_at` taken at `:2782` after the detector's pass already fired `_invalidate_tree_views(tree, changed_at=time.monotonic())` at `reckon/change_streams.py:453`; that read is a process-cache miss (`metadata_index.invalidate_tree`, reckon/metadata_index.py:338-344) and reaches `_reuse_covered` (:379, :429-434), so under §15's stated rule — "no invalidation from any other source … has reached the tree since that pass completed" — the record written by the pass is discarded for every streamed change and the ~2,500-stat sweep §15 exists to remove is paid on each one, while the section's own done-when (a direct `index_rows` read) and its live acceptance (a plain `/_index/reckon` GET) both pass and hide it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol §15 cites resolves at head: `_reuse_covered` (reckon/metadata_index.py:395) calls `covered_dir_identity` (:168) → `_dir_identity` (:879), `_fast_tree` (reckon/change_streams.py:414) calls `_invalidate_tree_views` at :453, and the arming branch at :427-434 does load the persisted stamps and return without stat-ing, exactly as §15 states; the cited 6.5 s first read and 11.3 s second read match §7's close comment in the same snapshot (line 273 and the §7 record naming "11.3 s on its second read", "The repair is §15").
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §15's four proof cases each carry their own control, and each control mutates a distinct piece of the guard (ignore the record; drop the moved directory from it; trust a disarmed or arming-pass record; trust the record regardless of its pass time), so each case can fail; the live acceptance is delimited to the second pass with the first reported as-is.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §15's node logs sit under the run directory with a revision header and an `EXIT=` last line, and the open first-read cost is recorded with §7's evidence under `docs/evidence/archive/the-page-paints-from-an-index-landed.html`, not in a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `_reuse_covered`, `_fast_tree`, `_dir_identity` and `tests/test_a_read_trusts_the_detector_pass.py` name the mechanism, with no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the new exemption names only the invalidation the pass itself fires, while the change stream's own read is preceded by a second invalidation the change-stream handler fires at `reckon/serve.py:2805`, from a source the same sentence classes as "any other source"; by the plan's own rule that read is untrusted and stats every recorded directory, so §15's benefit is absent on the read the exemption's parenthetical names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 carries one deliverable: reuse the change detector's recorded directory identities on the covered-set read instead of stat-ing every recorded directory.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §15's only declared dependency is `the-page-paints-from-an-index#s14` (`plan-section-depends-on`, snapshot line 29), which shares `reckon/metadata_index.py`, and its second write path `reckon/change_streams.py` needs no upstream section, so no declared relationship points at the wrong node.
